name: deep_nesting
description: A leaf four levels under an important goal vs. a leaf one level under an unimportant goal, same own importance. Forces the depth-decay decision: with no decay, the deep leaf's boost should not have eroded enough to lose.

nodes.label: Important goal, reached through a long chain
Leaf task, 4 levels under the important goal
Leaf task, 1 level under the unimportant goal, same own importance as task_deep

notes: The three middle nodes (program_l2, initiative_l3, epic_l4) are set to 0.03 -- see README.md's 'Design decisions' section for why no depth decay is the default; this fixture is what makes that decision actually testable. No-decay: task_deep = 0.1 + 3*0.03 + 0.9 = 1.09; task_shallow = 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3 -- task_deep wins, as stated. Halving-per-hop decay (0.5^hop_distance from the leaf): task_deep = 0.1 + 0.03*0.5 + 0.03*0.25 + 0.03*0.125 + 0.9*0.0625 = 0.1825; task_shallow = 0.1 + 0.2*0.5 = 0.2 -- the order flips, proving this fixture genuinely depends on no decay rather than merely tolerating a mild one (with the old 0.1 values it took a ~63%-per-hop decay to flip; 0.03 flips under a common 50%-per-hop decay). One-hop-only read: epic_l4 (0.03) alone still loses to goal_shallow_unimportant (0.2) alone, so a naive one-level-up implementation still gets the wrong answer under no-decay -- the fixture's original purpose still holds. Multiplicative (own * product of ancestor importances): task_deep = 0.1*0.03*0.03*0.03*0.9 ~= 0.0000024; task_shallow = 0.1*0.2 = 0.02 -- task_shallow still wins, same reversal as before, so the documented multiplicative assumption still holds.
